title.narrative: Second Secondary Education Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The SESDP II builds upon the education reforms supported by the Secondary Education Sector Development Program (SESDP). It introduces new features to improve the quality and relevance of secondary education, increase equitable access for disadvantaged adolescents, and strengthen education governance. These features include (i) pedagogically innovative school models; (ii) upgrading teacher standards; (iii) strengthening science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education; (iv) providing locally tailored vocational guidance; (v) targeted support to emerging disadvantaged groups; and (vi) strengthening local decision-making.

Progress Toward Outcome: a) PISA 2018: Viet Nam maintained high ratings and scores among performers. Due to Covid-19 situation, PISA 2021 is scheduled to take place in April-May 2022. Results will be published in 2023.
b) 2019 statistics show that the proportion of unemployed male and female youth aged 15-24 decreased to 43.6% for males, and 40.4% for females.
c) 2020 data indicates that 21.87% of university students study science & technology of which male and female achieved 27.03% and 16.71% respectively, increased by 2.5% and 3% as compared with 2017.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Nov 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/47140/47140-002-apfs-en_5.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1:1a. Model resource secondary schools and STEM developed and implemented in approximately 440 schools.1b. Professional teacher standards revised. More secondary teachers are using the upgraded teaching method and gender-sensitive STEM teaching approach in colleges.1c. Number of students in model resource secondary schools and STEM schools meeting acceptable standards on NAM is being monitored. NAM survey will be organized in April-May 2022.1d. School-based vocational knowledge and cognitive skills program introduced. Nearly 90% of the secondary teachers and principals are being evaluated by the revised nationwide system of assessment.1e. As of 2020, 1.7 million secondary students received market-related vocational and career orientation, of which 49% of beneficiary students are female.1f. TALIS 2018 data has been published for the use of policymakers.Output 2:2a. Number of migrant students in LS schools in SY 2020-2021: 14.618 students (77%) in the total of 18.945 migrant students attending secondary education. In 2020, the educational conditions of 21,816 disadvantage youth domestic migrants were recorded (female: 10,921; ethnicity: 3,248).2b. 33,6% of children with disabilities attended secondary schools at the right age. In 2020, total 18,945 disable youth attended LSE (increased by 40%) of which 8,775 are female and 2,833 are ethnic.Output 3:3a. Decentralization of secondary schooling through site-based decision-making promoted. Public expenditure and budgeting review of the secondary education subsector will be conducted in 2022.3b. The accountability mechanism in secondary schools has been strengthened which is reflected in the specific regulations on the rights and responsibilities of the principals and vice-principal of secondary schools. Surveys among teachers in selected beneficiary schools on site-based decision-making will be conducted.3c. 80% of model resource schools, districts, and provinces are expected to develop the assessment report on site-based decision-making.3d. PISA 2018 report will be issued in quarter 4/2021. PISA 2022 will take place and results to be available by 2023.3e. Data from grade 9 and 11 NAM for model resource and STEM schools, districts, and provinces will be analysed by December 2022 and national report available in 2023.
